name: Loaded March (Tab)
setup: Load a rucksack (bergen) to the prescribed weight, packed high and tight against your back, straps snug.
Wear broken-in boots or sturdy footwear and plan a measured route.
instructions: March at a brisk, sustainable pace — around 6 to 7 km/h on flat ground — driving through the full foot.
Stay tall under the load: chest up, shoulders back, core braced against the pack.
Take shorter, quicker steps uphill and controlled steps downhill.
Cover the prescribed distance or time; build weight and distance gradually week on week.

name: Casualty Drag
setup: Lay a heavy sandbag or drag dummy (training standard is around 110 kg, scale to ability) on a smooth, flat surface.
instructions: Grip the bag's handles or straps with both hands, facing away from the direction of travel.
Sit into a low position with your chest up and arms locked long.
Drive backward with powerful steps, leaning your bodyweight against the load.
Keep your spine neutral and your steps short and fast until the full distance is covered.

name: Jerry Can Carry
setup: Place a filled jerry can (or heavy dumbbell/kettlebell) beside each foot — the military standard is two 20 kg cans.
instructions: Deadlift both cans to standing with a flat back.
Walk the prescribed distance at a brisk, controlled pace, cans held at your sides.
Stay perfectly upright — no leaning, no swinging the cans.
Set the cans down with a flat back, rest as prescribed, and repeat.

name: Stretcher Carry
setup: Load a stretcher, litter or long bar to the prescribed weight. Work with a partner of similar height when carrying as a pair.
instructions: Squat down with a flat back and grip the handles at both ends.
Stand together on a count, keeping the stretcher level.
Walk the prescribed distance with short, synchronised steps, shoulders packed and core braced.
Lower together with control. Swap ends or hands each interval to balance the load.

name: Isometric Mid-Thigh Pull
setup: Set a barbell in a power rack at mid-thigh height and pin it so it cannot move (or load it far beyond your maximum).
Stand with the bar at mid-thigh, hands just outside your legs in an overhand grip.
instructions: Set a flat back, chest up, shoulders slightly over the bar — a strong deadlift lockout position.
Pull upward against the immovable bar as hard as possible for around 5 seconds.
Drive through your whole foot and keep your arms straight — the legs and hips produce the force.
Release gradually, never abruptly. Rest fully between efforts.

name: Seated Medicine Ball Power Throw
setup: Sit on the floor with your back and head flat against a wall, legs extended in front of you.
Hold a 4 kg medicine ball at your chest with both hands.
instructions: Keeping your back against the wall throughout, explosively press the ball up and out at roughly 45 degrees.
Throw as far as possible — the distance from the wall to first bounce is your score.
No rocking or leaning forward: all the power comes from your chest, shoulders and arms.
Take full rest between attempts and record your best.

name: Fireman's Carry
setup: Work with a partner of similar size, or use a heavy sandbag. Practise the lift unloaded first.
instructions: Squat and pull the partner's arm across your shoulders, ducking your head under so their torso lies across your upper back.
Wrap one arm behind their knee and grip their wrist with the same hand, locking the load to your shoulders.
Stand by driving through your legs with a neutral spine.
Walk the prescribed distance with short, stable steps, then lower them down with control.
